errors.what: Encoder fusion (ENC_FUSE=1) is mathematically equivalent but NOT bit-identical: enc weights drift ~1e-5 relative because cat([A,P]) changes the GRU kernel's reduction order.
Workflow harness failure: parallel[1] failed — agent StructuredOutput retry cap (5) exceeded, 5 failed calls with no valid output (1 of 9 agents lost).

D_MODEL_B is read by NOTHING in self_organize.py (which reads D_MODEL). Every direct `python3 self_organize.py` silently ran at d=128 instead of 768 — including the entire first A100 bench AND the pilot command Claude had given the researcher. Param counts prove it: 4,309,760 = '4.3M', 5,069,312 = '5.1M'.
STREAM_LEN is counted in BYTES while the training loop iterates a TOKEN stream (~1.84 B/tok), so STEPS=1800 silently ran 976 steps.

WRITE_TARGET=0.12 not honored: the additive adaptive gate pins gate_theta at gate_ceil=0.95 within ~40 calls, so kept fraction runs 1.00->0.93->0.80 and the store hits MEM_CAP=200,000 by step ~831 instead of the predicted 6,510.
WRITE_QUANTILE was not wired to the EditableMemory constructor, making the first gate A/B meaningless.

English-only (single-domain) runs crash AFTER training with IndexError: Cannot choose from an empty sequence at self_organize.py:1317 — the wrongness-injection test needs >=2 processes. Killed generation, unlearn and verification.

Audit critical: the expert-independence test calls fab.remove() on the BUSIEST expert and never restores it, so every eval after that point — including the generation samples used to judge coherence — ran on a mutilated model.

Audit critical: fab.cent was a plain attribute, not a registered buffer, so with ROUTE_GROUNDED=1 the centroids that ARE the routing function were never saved, resumed, or moved to GPU — prompt.py routed every generation with untrained centroids.

Audit critical: EXPERTS=1 is a complete no-op when FABRIC=1 (elif chain at :1030-1040); adapters get zero gradient, verified 'adapters learned: -0.000', while the end-of-run report still prints expert counts. bpb_true has the same precedence so no test could catch it.
Audit critical: CORPUS_CAP defaults to 2 MB and run_full_unfrozen.sh never sets it — a multi-day run would have trained on 2 MB of English.
Audit critical: EPOCHS>1 only resamples under DISK_STREAM=1; otherwise every epoch is a byte-identical replay. Both default off in the product script.
_save_ckpt was non-atomic: a kill mid-save destroyed the only checkpoint and the tokenizer that decodes it.
Self-inflicted #1: the new startup-guard block referenced EPOCHS before assignment -> UnboundLocalError.
Self-inflicted #2: ablation restore used load_state_dict, which cannot repopulate a ModuleList that remove() shrank -> RuntimeError on unexpected keys.

mem.pos provenance was written as arange(bpos, bpos+WIN) — bpos is a BYTE coordinate but arange steps once per TOKEN (~1.85 B/tok), so recorded provenance drifted 200+ bytes over a WIN=256 window while prompt.py's _recall reads only a 220-byte span. Every grounded passage lookup pointed at the wrong text.
Self-inflicted #3: a prefix string-replace swallowed the `_fab_nov = torch.full(...)` assignment into a comment -> UnboundLocalError.
Self-inflicted #4: a smart quote (U+201D) introduced by a patch script -> SyntaxError at line 350.

Fabric.remove(j) rebuilt bodies/keys/qproj but never pruned cent, so every expert above index j was routed by its neighbour's region — silently misrouting the whole population after any removal, and corrupting the independence test.

ROUTE_T=1.0 with 64-d unit vectors gives cosine logits of std ~0.125, so the top-vs-mean routing weight ratio is ~1.37x AT ANY N — effectively uniform, so top-k selects noise and no expert can specialize. Likely explains the historical '0 exclusive experts' and '12/17 idle'.
Burst births were exact clones: grow() seeds the newborn centroid at the current signature, so a burst of 3 created three identical regions that could never differentiate.

Tool use rejected by user, then container restarted. Two background tasks lost: 'Rerun A/B with knob wired' (bsevl3kt2) and 'Full English-only end-to-end run' (b7vyte2ud). The partition-vs-capacity isolation test had to be re-run.

Checkpoint/resume did not carry own/last/tick/n_own/quota, and the existing restore path COMPACTS entries into the first N slots — which would have silently reassigned every entry to the wrong owner block and destroyed the partition on resume.

requirements.txt pinned torch>=2.1, which on linux-aarch64 is satisfied by a CPU-ONLY wheel (every CUDA dep gated platform_machine==x86_64 through 2.10.0). It imports cleanly, reports no GPU, and would have trained on the Grace CPU while merely looking slow.

Memory blend rule broken: hp = dist.sum() but read() scatters a softmax, so dist always sums to exactly 1.0 and hp is identically 1.0 — an unconditional 50/50 model/memory mix at every position regardless of match quality, while `conf` was computed and discarded by every caller.

LAYERS=12 blockers: TransformerEncoder lacked a final LayerNorm with norm_first=True (checkpoints would load into a different network); selfcheck built a 12-layer autograd graph over every stored entry (tens of GiB); FAB_HID_MULT not float-parsed.

prompt.py's fabric used the NON-GROUNDED routing path (q_entry/keys) while training routes by centroid cosine — and in grounded mode those parameters receive no gradient at all. It also blended hidden states while training ensembles at the output. Third distinct defect in the generation path.
Self-inflicted #5: making FAB_HID_MULT float-parsed made hid = hid_mult*d a float -> nn.Linear TypeError.
BENCH=1 returns before the end-of-run save, so SAVE_CKPT alone writes nothing — a bench run produces no checkpoint unless CKPT_EVERY is set.
Bash error '(${$(date +%s)}s): bad substitution' killed the scaling-study loop after only one of three configs.
Self-inflicted #6: the KEY_LAYERS module-level constant was inserted between @torch.no_grad() and its function -> SyntaxError.

DomainAssembler over-segmentation: four rules disagree about what a domain is. _assign queries a SINGLE 128-byte window against 40-window centroid means with absolute NEW_DIST=0.35; create at 0.35 vs merge at 0.12 leaves a permanent dead zone; `size` is cumulative so any domain reaching 15 windows is immortal; MANAGE_STALE=2000 exceeded the pilot's 937 total steps so ZERO culls ever ran; and domains were the only uncapped population. asm.manage is O(N^2) and asm.rekey does N sequential GRU passes — combined they double wall-clock at N~300.

The completeness metric Claude added specifically to stop over-segmentation hiding was itself wrong — it computed H(true|domain), which is HOMOGENEITY and behaves like purity. The run reporting 'completeness 0.89 | V 0.91' was not the good result it appeared to be.
Claude's own suggested launch command omitted DATA_MODE=real, so it fell through to synthetic mode where TOK is never constructed and died later inside _retok with a bare AttributeError.

[profile] attribution percentage divided a WINDOW's instrumented time by the WHOLE run's elapsed time (_prof is cleared at every [rate] print). Reported 97%/32%/42%/24% 'of wall-clock attributed' were meaningless; component shares were always correct.

Adaptive encoder warmup stopped at 3001 of 30000 steps reading a plateau, but separation had FALLEN from its random-init 0.24 to 0.08 and only partially recovered to 0.18 — the early-stop fired on what is arguably a collapse.
fetch_data.sh line 69/71: 'bc: command not found' on the GH200, so all corpus sizes printed as 0.0 MB.

Final 4-domain GH200 run: 0/74 live domains GENUINE (mean silhouette -0.22, 67 live tiny), 142 domains for 4 processes, V-measure 0.42. Also the online tokenizer stalled at vocab 512/16384 with '+0 since last retok' in both GPU runs.

Pattern worth flagging for synthesis: this window contains an unusually dense retraction chain on ONE question — domain assembly. The sequence is (1) "domain assembly is failing" -> retracted, it was a 2-domain config artifact; (2) "undertraining confirmed decisively, purity 0.54->0.96" -> retracted, purity is gameable by fragmentation and the assembler partitions by splice segment; (3) after the rewrite, "completeness 0.89 / V 0.91" -> retracted, the completeness formula was homogeneity and the 64 was just MAX_DOMAINS binding. Second pattern: six self-inflicted build breaks in this window (EPOCHS ordering, load_state_dict on a shrunk ModuleList, a prefix match commenting out _fab_nov, a smart quote, FAB_HID_MULT float, the KEY_LAYERS constant between decorator and function).
